people.role: Founder (1150) and head of Chức Hà Các; weaves fire-silk without the vents
people.appearance: A tall, quick woman with burn-pale fingertips and a red shuttle stuck through her hair like a pin.
people.backstory: Thân Vân Cẩm was born in 1110 to a weaving house of Tang Điền, where the mulberry has fed the south's silkworms since 200 (A300). The town's weavers descend from the reelers who fled Hỏa Ti Trấn when it burned in 590 (V165), and they have never stopped wanting the fire-silk back. Her mother Hầu Tố Cẩm (hau_to_cam) tried to put fire into silk with her own Fire, burned her hands to the bone, and died in 1148. Thân made a method of it and in 1150 founded the pavilion with weavers sworn to the palace (V172): fire-silk from Tang Điền's worms, woven without the vents, keeping the letter of the founder's vow. It holds a season, then chars. The palace's treasurer Vưu Cẩm Thư (vuu_cam_thu) buys it at a price that hurts, and her factor Chiêm Lợi Châu (chiem_loi_chau) beats the price down further. The array keeper Tang Kế Ti (tang_ke_ti) splices it into the Nest Array in secret and owes her for it. Tang's son Tang Tục Lạc (tang_tuc_lac) carries it, and Thân loves him. Last autumn he asked her to marry him, and this spring his mother named the dowry.
people.wants: Silk that lasts: a banner to equal the Xích Hà Kỳ, hung in the palace's Hall of Virtue with her name on it; and Tang Tục Lạc, on whatever terms his mother names.
people.secret: Last winter Tang Tục Lạc brought her one strand of his mother's new silk to compare. It was reeled at the vent, against the founder's vow, and she has kept it, so she knows what the dowry is for. She means to say yes. Since spring she has cut the outer gate's rice by a third against the sixty dowry years, and tells the girls it is the palace's price.

people.role: Guest elder: the indigo dyer of Lam Điện, hired for the pavilion's colours
people.appearance: An old woman with hands dyed blue to the wrist, who smells of indigo vats.
people.backstory: The dyers of Lam Điện are the grandchildren of Kim Sa Trấn, which a storm tide drowned in 913 (V171). Nhiễm Thanh Lam is the best of them and the only Kết Đan. Thân Vân Cẩm (than_van_cam) hired her in 1152 to give the pavilion's silk colours that hold. She takes no part in the pavilion's quarrels, is never taught its methods, and outranks its head by a realm.

people.role: Elder of the worm sheds; cousin of the palace's array keeper
people.appearance: A small, careful woman who carries silkworms in her sleeve to keep them warm.
people.backstory: Of the Tang reeler family of Tang Điền, cousin of the palace's array keeper Tang Kế Ti (tang_ke_ti), whose line went up to the Fire Court with Tang Sơ Ti in 592 while hers stayed with the worms. She keeps the pavilion's sheds, reweaves the Robe of the First Weave every season, and keeps the founder's vow stricter than anyone. Since her cousin named the dowry she has packed the northern bolts under the leaf-pickers' baskets herself, because sixty years at the palace's price would starve her sheds.

people.backstory: A weaver of Tang Điền who spent forty years trying to weave fire-silk without the vents, running her own Fire into the thread with no method to guide it. She burned her hands to the bone in 1146 and died of the burns two years later. Her daughter Thân Vân Cẩm (than_van_cam) made the method from her notes and founded the pavilion in 1150 (V172).
